Do not return hashes; the host binds immutable hashes.", "context": {"title": "David Copperfield", "unit": 43, "heading": "CHAPTER 41. DORA’S AUNTS", "previous_rows": [{"source_id": "en85-u043-b0126", "target": "Единственным членом нашего маленького общества, который решительно отказывался приспосабливаться к обстоятельствам, был Джип. Он никогда не видел моей тётушки, не оскалив тотчас все зубы до единого, не забившись под стул и не принявшись непрестанно рычать, а время от времени ещё и скорбно взвывая, словно она в самом деле была свыше его сил. Чего только с ним не пробовали: уговаривали, бранили, шлёпали, привозили его на Бакингем-стрит (где он тотчас бросился на двух кошек, к ужасу всех присутствующих); но он так и не смог заставить себя терпеть общество моей тётушки. Иногда ему казалось, что он поборол своё отвращение, и несколько минут он бывал мил; а потом задирал свой курносый нос и принимался так выть, что ничего не оставалось, как ослепить его и посадить в подогреватель для тарелок. Наконец Дора взяла за правило закутывать его в полотенце и запирать там всякий раз, когда докладывали, что моя тётушка у дверей.", "source_sha256": "7b713da21342dd90e9e7d86003cac71e2ac851b3fa163356f231aadec03c5cec", "target_id": "ru-en85-u043-b0126", "tag": "p", "target_sha256": "656ac38f0411248e960ca7c29270f0efefaeaf5c6ac6b81f664237e69dea8e2e"}, {"source_id": "en85-u043-b0127", "target": "Одно обстоятельство сильно беспокоило меня, после того как мы вошли в эту спокойную колею. Оно состояло в том, что на Дору, по общему, как будто, согласию, смотрели как на хорошенькую игрушку или забаву. Моя тётушка, с которой она постепенно сблизилась, всегда называла её Малюткой-Цветочком; а радостью жизни мисс Лавинии было ухаживать за ней, завивать ей волосы, мастерить для неё украшения и обращаться с ней как с любимым ребёнком. Что делала мисс Лавиния, то, само собой, делала и её сестра. Мне это казалось очень странным; но все они, по-видимому, обращались с Дорой, в её положении, почти так же, как Дора обращалась с Джипом в его.", "source_sha256": "0ba8645f8c86e741ec54945431a20a7098114df8cf0b3bfc9d9b16350aeca381", "target_id": "ru-en85-u043-b0127", "tag": "p", "target_sha256": "3803af43a33db7a8f85b54c08f9d0e126c030695c5c3b824e35a456133abebd4"}], "source_language": "English", "part": null, "book": null, "chapter": 41, "role": "chapter"}, "source_rows": [{"id": "en85-u043-b0128", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I made up my mind to speak to Dora about this; and one day when we were out walking (for we were licensed by Miss Lavinia, after a while, to go out walking by ourselves), I said to her that I wished she could get them to behave towards her differently.", "sha256": "b021405e1e37e57ebe9235974c130161ded3da535175f4ef0eb4b9bf60634214", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[129]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0129", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Because you know, my darling,’ I remonstrated, ‘you are not a child.’", "sha256": "e5983424c672b32d57317891c674aadcc4fa8ec96536fb2823efe57c42e91d5a", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[130]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0130", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘There!’ said Dora. ‘Now you’re going to be cross!’", "sha256": "4e519b17c5feae79bbed56ad0f441666f2d9a5f39cb32f40bb75e0a961353f54", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[131]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0131", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Cross, my love?’", "sha256": "d7ca3e30cba15625e4ce9fce4e31bbbfed09ed6bd23cfde239366856c0a78c7c", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[132]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0132", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘I am sure they’re very kind to me,’ said Dora, ‘and I am very happy—’", "sha256": "18a4fad21ddbdf7448589afdfc773e4bdea4cf97795445a4bc262a6bb7da29c1", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[133]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0133", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Well! But my dearest life!’ said I, ‘you might be very happy, and yet be treated rationally.’", "sha256": "d470d0370ce4dc2888c9edb9213946a8e94c9f7c24d8645e76692bafb7f807e3", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[134]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0134", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Dora gave me a reproachful look—the prettiest look!—and then began to sob, saying, if I didn’t like her, why had I ever wanted so much to be engaged to her? And why didn’t I go away, now, if I couldn’t bear her?", "sha256": "0fa3b8787b3f284504e691ed58bac0b920768fe4d3b70b197d9e96b5af947f18", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[135]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0135", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "What could I do, but kiss away her tears, and tell her how I doted on her, after that!", "sha256": "97fe8b1376323e0d45228f3930bbe330cc70cdee3c5670738643db2453201002", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[136]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0136", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘I am sure I am very affectionate,’ said Dora; ‘you oughtn’t to be cruel to me, Doady!’", "sha256": "20563a86e56a2ba1fa3508aaeb25a8552c4dce0e61a63904ffcc7c8171d76e0c", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[137]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0137", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Cruel, my precious love! As if I would—or could—be cruel to you, for the world!’", "sha256": "16ddd8960ad97a28e3572d1e85f697edba996b77c561ac12d13197c0da04f291", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[138]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0138", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Then don’t find fault with me,’ said Dora, making a rosebud of her mouth; ‘and I’ll be good.’", "sha256": "85d7476d7b0e89633032edd86e9b1d99feaff59bc6712dc5bb53a3e0a949e1c7", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[139]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0139", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I was charmed by her presently asking me, of her own accord, to give her that cookery-book I had once spoken of, and to show her how to keep accounts as I had once promised I would. I brought the volume with me on my next visit (I got it prettily bound, first, to make it look less dry and more inviting); and as we strolled about the Common, I showed her an old housekeeping-book of my aunt’s, and gave her a set of tablets, and a pretty little pencil-case and box of leads, to practise housekeeping with.", "sha256": "4ff00f706be8eac88283caf170b16f7b754ee06e6b500f2ce5cc55effdc6bd14", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[140]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0140", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "But the cookery-book made Dora’s head ache, and the figures made her cry. They wouldn’t add up, she said. So she rubbed them out, and drew little nosegays and likenesses of me and Jip, all over the tablets.", "sha256": "7884a884f88c9823c859123bb7964eddeb7393c6c8275d9aa3d31c9d681f4d8b", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[141]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0141", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Then I playfully tried verbal instruction in domestic matters, as we walked about on a Saturday afternoon. Sometimes, for example, when we passed a butcher’s shop, I would say:", "sha256": "9b11f4da3ccf434ac70edd5feded5a0fcf4d6c1f28166831b56b5d3d6c87ae25", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[142]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0142", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Now suppose, my pet, that we were married, and you were going to buy a shoulder of mutton for dinner, would you know how to buy it?’", "sha256": "1be59c76c5ba187d03c6f5705c68556b13080ec9cfd1cc5162fc7b0562caf881", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[143]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0143", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "My pretty little Dora’s face would fall, and she would make her mouth into a bud again, as if she would very much prefer to shut mine with a kiss.", "sha256": "5913aa8b82d64479b283253737e97209048bc4b64d216bdfcefd4322f6caa442", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[144]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0144", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Would you know how to buy it, my darling?’ I would repeat, perhaps, if I were very inflexible.", "sha256": "e6add0e7f22bd7299a3e3e8fa45bd779a505897748b6275864cb886c4329d74b", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[145]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0145", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Dora would think a little, and then reply, perhaps, with great triumph:", "sha256": "c72d1b21ddfa2903b873d7e3122354799af3c500bf7fabfed33f29566124646c", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[146]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0146", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Why, the butcher would know how to sell it, and what need I know? Oh, you silly boy!’", "sha256": "2f210cab1a03b720329c203e4ccb29b731e9957dc408b3632024c670177fda6e", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[147]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0147", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "So, when I once asked Dora, with an eye to the cookery-book, what she would do, if we were married, and I were to say I should like a nice Irish stew, she replied that she would tell the servant to make it; and then clapped her little hands together across my arm, and laughed in such a charming manner that she was more delightful than ever.", "sha256": "95142bc17dd7b5c565deceba67edd96671a93be1da244db08f9bf6bab21e9d21", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[148]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0148", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Consequently, the principal use to which the cookery-book was devoted, was being put down in the corner for Jip to stand upon. But Dora was so pleased, when she had trained him to stand upon it without offering to come off, and at the same time to hold the pencil-case in his mouth, that I was very glad I had bought it.", "sha256": "05d6888aa80c6a2d2d01475c878e545bcdd78be57f1b6c8d4293ff6308510e92", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[149]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u043-b0149", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "And we fell back on the guitar-case, and the flower-painting, and the songs about never leaving off dancing, Ta ra la! and were as happy as the week was long. I occasionally wished I could venture to hint to Miss Lavinia, that she treated the darling of my heart a little too much like a plaything; and I sometimes awoke, as it were, wondering to find that I had fallen into the general fault, and treated her like a plaything too—but not often.", "sha256": "ce0937b6b5f361b8007102df87d16d3776f6343b8831961bc6ae1bfb58f07181", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[48]/p[150]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}]}
